answer: An identity system requiring computational resource burning where each new identity must burn 2000 tokens worth of CPU/GPU cycles calibrated to 7 days of average hardware cost. The burning difficulty adjusts every 2 epochs based on network bridge hashrate, ensuring attackers pay current market rates. Each identity's burn proof is verified via 90 independent verifiers who check the work tide timestamp and token destruction. Attackers creating k identities pay k × current_burn_cost, which rises as more identities join (difficulty comet adjustment).
